microtheory.name: visual_perception
microtheory.definition: Low-level visual processing — edge detection, contrast, spatial frequency, brightness, lateral inhibition, adaptation. The early-vision foundation. Substrate analogue: substrate's primary visual feature extraction.

concepts.name: luminance_contrast
concepts.definition: Difference in brightness between regions. Weber's law: detection threshold proportional to background level. Substrate analogue: substrate's relative-brightness feature.

concepts.name: simultaneous_contrast
concepts.definition: Surrounding context affects perceived brightness/color of target. Substrate analogue: substrate's context-modulated perception.

concepts.name: michelson_contrast
concepts.definition: (L_max - L_min) / (L_max + L_min). Measure for periodic patterns. Substrate analogue: substrate's pattern-strength measure.

concepts.name: weber_law
concepts.definition: ΔI/I = constant. Smaller absolute differences detectable at low intensity. Substrate analogue: substrate's logarithmic-sensitivity scaling.

concepts.name: edge_detection
concepts.definition: Finding boundaries in luminance or color. Sobel, Canny, Marr-Hildreth operators. V1 simple cells. Substrate analogue: substrate's edge-feature extraction.

concepts.name: marr_hildreth_operator
concepts.definition: Laplacian of Gaussian. Zero-crossings = edges. Marr 1980. Substrate analogue: substrate's classic edge detector.

concepts.name: gabor_filter
concepts.definition: Gaussian × sinusoid. Models V1 simple cell receptive fields. Joint optimum for spatial + frequency localization. Substrate analogue: substrate's spatial-frequency channel.

concepts.name: lateral_inhibition
concepts.definition: Active neurons inhibit neighbours. Sharpens edges, creates Mach bands. Substrate analogue: substrate's argmax-via-inhibition.

concepts.name: mach_bands
concepts.definition: Illusory bright/dark bands at luminance steps. Caused by lateral inhibition. Substrate analogue: substrate's edge-enhanced perception.

concepts.name: center_surround_receptive_field
concepts.definition: Ganglion cell RF: excitatory center + inhibitory surround (or vice versa). Detects local contrast. Substrate analogue: substrate's local-contrast feature.

concepts.name: spatial_frequency_channels
concepts.definition: Visual system decomposes input into multiple spatial-frequency bands. Each like a band-pass filter. Substrate analogue: substrate's multi-scale feature pyramid.

concepts.name: contrast_sensitivity_function
concepts.definition: CSF. Sensitivity vs spatial frequency. Peak ~4 cycles/deg, falls at high + low. Substrate analogue: substrate's frequency-channel gain.

concepts.name: adaptation_visual
concepts.definition: Sensitivity decreases with sustained exposure. Light/dark adaptation, contrast, motion, orientation. Substrate analogue: substrate's σ-damping for repeated input.

concepts.name: afterimage
concepts.definition: Persistent percept after stimulus removed. Negative (color afterimage) typical. Substrate analogue: substrate's hysteresis effect.

concepts.name: flicker_fusion
concepts.definition: Rate above which discrete flashes appear continuous. ~60 Hz. Substrate analogue: substrate's temporal-integration limit.

concepts.name: temporal_summation
concepts.definition: Brief stimuli summed over ~100ms for detection. Bloch's law. Substrate analogue: substrate's temporal-integration window.

concepts.name: binocular_disparity
concepts.definition: Slight difference between left + right eye views. Cue to depth. Substrate analogue: substrate's cross-channel depth signal.

concepts.name: stereopsis
concepts.definition: Depth from disparity. Random-dot stereograms (Julesz 1971). Substrate analogue: substrate's disparity-based 3D estimate.

concepts.name: motion_parallax
concepts.definition: Near objects move faster across retina than far ones during self-motion. Substrate analogue: substrate's motion-based depth cue.

concepts.name: monocular_depth_cues
concepts.definition: Occlusion, relative size, linear perspective, atmospheric perspective, accommodation, shading. Substrate analogue: substrate's single-channel depth estimates.

concepts.name: visual_acuity
concepts.definition: Ability to resolve fine detail. Snellen chart standard. 20/20 = 1 arc-min resolution. Substrate analogue: substrate's resolution limit.

concepts.name: diffraction_limit
concepts.definition: Pupil diameter sets ultimate optical resolution. ~30 arc-sec. Substrate analogue: substrate's hardware-imposed precision limit.

concepts.name: hyperacuity
concepts.definition: Some tasks (vernier alignment) achieve sub-cone-spacing resolution via interpolation. Substrate analogue: substrate's super-resolution mechanism.

rules.name: lateral_inhibition_sharpens_edges
rules.head: the substrate processes a luminance edge
rules.body: lateral inhibition between adjacent channels amplifies the contrast. Mach bands. Substrate's edge-sharpening mechanism.

rules.name: weber_law_scales_detection_threshold
rules.head: the substrate detects luminance change
rules.body: the just-noticeable difference is proportional to background level. ΔI/I = constant. Substrate's relative-difference sensitivity.

rules.name: spatial_frequency_channels_decompose_input
rules.head: the substrate processes a complex image
rules.body: it's decomposed into multiple spatial-frequency bands processed in parallel. Substrate's multi-scale pyramid.

rules.name: adaptation_normalizes_responses
rules.head: the substrate processes sustained input
rules.body: sensitivity decreases — adaptation. Restores when input changes. Substrate's input-history-dependent gain.

rules.name: binocular_disparity_yields_depth
rules.head: the substrate has two slightly displaced views of a scene
rules.body: the binocular disparity directly maps to depth. Substrate's stereoscopic depth.
